extraction.name: IFEval (Instruction-Following Evaluation)
extraction.description: A benchmark for evaluating the instruction-following ability of large language models using verifiable instructions. The benchmark contains around 500 prompts with 25 types of verifiable instructions that can be automatically and objectively verified.
extraction.creator: Jeffrey Zhou, Tianjian Lu, Swaroop Mishra, Siddhartha Brahma, Sujoy Basu, Yi Luan, Denny Zhou, Le Hou
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Prompts were generated through a four-step process: generating base prompts with randomly selected verifiable instructions, using few-shot prompting to identify and remove illogical prompts, applying few-shot prompting to rephrase prompts for diversity, and manually checking and editing each rephrased prompt.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Base prompts generated with randomly selected verifiable instructions from 25 identified types of verifiable instructions.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: GPT-4 responses collected in November 2023, PaLM 2 S responses collected in August 2023
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Few-shot prompting was used to identify and remove illogical prompts, and to rephrase prompts for increased diversity.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Manual checking and editing of all rephrased prompts. Response transformations applied for loose accuracy metric including removing markdown font modifiers, removing first/last lines.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Responses are automatically verified against verifiable instructions using deterministic programs. Each instruction has a verification function that checks if the instruction is followed.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Two accuracy metrics are computed: strict accuracy using exact verification, and loose accuracy applying transformations to reduce false negatives while potentially introducing false positives.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Few-shot prompting for prompt generation and filtering, deterministic verification programs for instruction-following evaluation
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark aims to improve evaluation of LLM instruction-following capabilities, which is crucial for safety and reliability of LLM implementations, especially in critical scenarios like healthcare or autonomous systems.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Very few instructions are 100% verifiable objectively and automatically - edge cases exist where it is hard to determine if an instruction is followed. The verification approach may have false negatives (strict metric) or false positives (loose metric). The current implementation focuses on verifiable instructions which may not cover all real-world instruction-following scenarios.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Evaluating the instruction-following ability of large language models. The benchmark enables automatic and objective assessment of how well models follow specific types of instructions, and allows comparison of different LLMs across various instruction types.

name.evidence: we introduce Instruction-Following Eval ( IFEval ) for large language models.

description.evidence: IFEval is a straightforward and easy-to-reproduce evaluation benchmark. It focuses on a set of "verifiable instructions" such as "write in more than 400 words" and "mention the keyword of AI at least 3 times". We identified 25 types of those verifiable instructions and constructed around 500 prompts, with each prompt containing one or more verifiable instructions.

Finally, we manually check and edit the rephrased prompts one by one.

rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: The capability of LLMs to accurately interpret and follow natural language instructions is crucial, not only for the precision of tasks but also for the safety and reliability of their implementations. Discrepancies or misunderstandings in following instructions can lead to unintended outputs, which might have dire results, especially in crucial scenarios like healthcare or autonomous systems.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: we introduce Instruction-Following Eval ( IFEval ) for large language models. IFEval is a straightforward and easy-to-reproduce evaluation benchmark. ... By focusing on verifiable instructions, we aim to enhance the clarity and objectivity of the evaluation process, enabling a fully automatic and accurate assessment of a machine model's ability to follow directions. Furthermore, by analyzing the evaluation results, researchers are able to draw insights on what types of instructions are not usually followed, and compare different large language models on various instruction types.
